title: Why did the concurrency test fail once under full-suite parallel load?
statement: What caused the single observed failure of the separate-process concurrency test during a full parallel run on 2026-08-18, and is serialisation implicated at all?
notes: Reopening condition: any recurrence after the fix. Bounded non-reproduction only — 80 post-fix runs across three cells, which at a 10% per-run rate would miss a recurrence about 4% of the time. AST-0003 stands refuted for the pre-fix code and is now scoped to say so.
answer: Lock acquisition, not serialisation. openSync(lockPath,'wx') returned EPERM rather than EEXIST under contention on Windows, and the retry loop keyed only on EEXIST, so a transient was treated as fatal. Reproduced and classified on run 19 of a declared 40: one child of six failed in 507ms with EPERM, the other five allocated distinct IDs, and no duplicate ID occurred. Serialisation was never implicated. The maxWaitMs 10s->30s mitigation applied on 2026-08-18 addressed a timeout that did not happen and has been reverted. Fix: retry EEXIST/EPERM/EBUSY/EACCES on acquisition, the same family as #72's rename retry.
